Class NativeHttpServer

java.lang.Object
io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.internal.NativeHttpServer
public final class NativeHttpServer extends Object
The board's single-connection HTTP and HTTPS listener behind the board-side com.sun.net.httpserver API. A program serves requests with com.sun.net.httpserver.HttpServer or HttpsServer instead; Juno's own WifiProvisioner answers with respond(int, String, String) directly. Each method is a compiler intrinsic with no body on the JVM.

begin(int) or beginTls(int, byte[], int, byte[], int) starts listening once. accept(byte[], int) returns -1 at once when no client is waiting, or reads one complete request (method, path, headers and body) within a fixed five-second deadline. After a successful accept(), method(), path(), contentLength() and header(String, byte[], int) describe that request, and one response must close the connection before the next accept().

  • Method Details

    • begin

      public static void begin(int port)
      Starts listening for plain HTTP on port, once Wi-Fi is connected or an access point is up.

    • beginTls

      public static boolean beginTls(int port, byte[] certificate, int certificateLength, byte[] privateKey, int privateKeyLength)
      Starts listening for HTTPS on port, presenting certificate (PEM) and proving it with privateKey (PEM, or PKCS#8 or SEC1 DER). The buffers are parsed here and can be wiped afterwards. Returns false when the certificate or key does not parse. ESP32 boards, the Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W and the Portenta H7 only.

    • accept

      public static int accept(byte[] bodyBuffer, int bodyBufferLength)

    • method

      public static String method()

      public static String path()

    • contentLength

    • header

      public static int header(String name, byte[] buffer, int bufferLength)
      Copies the value of request header name, matched case-insensitively with spaces around the value trimmed, into buffer and returns its length, or -1 when the request has no such header. Only the first 384 bytes of the request's header lines are kept.

    • respond

      public static void respond(int status, String contentType, String body)
      Replies with body, then closes the connection; contentType must be a string literal.
